profile.headline: Software Engineer at Mathworks
profile.summary: My focus at MathWorks is enhancing the efficiency of embedded C++ generated code from MATLAB and Simulink. In particular I work in data parallelization which benefits domains like deep learning, image processing, and others.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer for Embedded Coder Efficiency
positions.description:
• Worked on C++ code generation from Simulink/MATLAB to support PyTorch and TensorFlow models, contributing performance enhancements via upstream patches to LLVM and torch-mlir.

• Developed a reinforcement learning–based autoscheduler in PyTorch to automatically discover efficient compiler optimization sequences.

• Worked on runtime performance improvement for generated C++ code for deep learning, image processing, and computer vision leveraging Halide and MLIR.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer in Simulink Embedded Coder
positions.description:
• Implemented multi-dimensional array support in Simulink Embedded Coder, enabling more flexible and efficient C/C++ code generation.

• Added row-major memory layout support for MATLAB Function blocks in Simulink, improving integration with C/C++ code and enhancing performance for embedded applications.

positions.title: Software Engineer for AUTOSAR C/C++ code generation
positions.description:
• Developed and shipped key AUTOSAR C/C++ code generation features at MathWorks, including a Simulink signal invalidation block and improved support for inter-runnable variables via rate transition blocks.

• Refactored AUTOSAR code generation infrastructure to improve modularity, data flow, and maintainability—reducing muda (waste) and streamlining future feature integration.

• Contributed to AUTOSAR mapping and code generation for startup/shutdown subsystems and runnables; implemented support for JMAAB Type B architecture and enhanced Simulink root inport mapping with new AUTOSAR receiver port modes.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer in Test
positions.description:
• Designed and implemented enhancements to model randomization and verification tools at MathWorks, including parallel build support and code generation determinism for improved testing robustness.

• Awarded a patent for innovations in model randomization.

• Delivered production features in Simulink Embedded Coder to improve the quality, performance, and maintainability of generated C/C++ code.

positions.title: Digital Design/Verification Engineer II
positions.description: • Developed SystemVerilog test environments using the AVM (Advanced Verification Methodology) framework for verification of Orion CEV TT Ethernet data/physical layers, 3D graphics instruction processor, and NVM bridge HDL components.
positions.insights: Skills: VHDL · Unified Modeling Language (UML) · Python · Software Engineering · Software Development · Linux · Six Sigma · Verilog

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Developed a J2EE/Struts-based web application for managing engine parts data at Pratt & Whitney, delivering a full-stack solution from front-end UI to backend database.

• Designed and implemented front-end interfaces, business logic, data persistence layer, and comprehensive unit tests to ensure reliability and maintainability.

• Collaborated with cross-functional teams to integrate the application seamlessly into existing workflows and systems.

• Optimized data retrieval and processing, significantly improving user experience and operational efficiency.
positions.insights: Skills: Java · XML · JavaServer Pages (JSP) · JavaScript · SQL · Unified Modeling Language (UML) · Python · Software Engineering · J2EE · Software Development

patents.title: Determining functional equivalence of configurations of a model
patents.description: A method may comprise determining, by executing a first model having first configuration parameters, a first result associated with the first model. The method may comprise determining, by executing a second model having second configuration parameters, a second result associated with the second model. The method may comprise determining, based on the first result, the second result, and equivalency criteria, that the second model is not functionally equivalent to the first model. The equivalency criteria may indicate that the second model is functionally equivalent to the first model when a difference between the second result and the first result satisfies a threshold. The method may comprise modifying a configuration parameter, of the second configuration parameters, to cause the second model to improve toward functional equivalence with the first model.
